message.content:
Sure! Below is a quick guide (and two short snippets) showing how you could post that comment to **VirusTotal** via its REST API.  
Just copy‑paste one of the snippets into your terminal / IDE, swap out the placeholder values (`YOUR_API_KEY`, `IP_ADDRESS`) with what you already have, and hit *Enter*.

---

### Quick checklist before running:

| Item | What to put |
|------|-------------|
| **API Key** | Your real VT key – e.g., `ABC321` |
| **Target IP** | The IP you’re commenting on – e.g., `192.168.1.1` |
| **Comment text** | `"Confirmed #malware"` |

> ⚠️ Make sure you keep your API key secret; don’t share it publicly!

---

## Option A – Using `curl`

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

API_KEY="ABC321"
TARGET_IP="192.168.1.1"

JSON_PAYLOAD='{
    "type":"comment",
    "attributes":{
        "text":"Confirmed #malware"
    }
}'

curl -X POST \
     https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/"$TARGET_IP"/comments \
     -H "x-apikey: $API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --data "$JSON_PAYLOAD"
```

Run this from a shell. If everything goes well you’ll see a JSON response containing the newly created comment’s ID and other metadata.

---

## Option B – Using Python (`requests`)

```python
import requests
import json

api_key   = "ABC321"
ip_address= "192.168.1.1"

url = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{ip_address}/comments"

payload = {
    "type": "comment",
    "attributes": {
        "text": "Confirmed #malware"
    }
}

headers = {
    "x-apikey": api_key,
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}

response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, data=json.dumps(payload))

print("Status:", response.status_code)
print("Response body:")
print(response.json())
```

Make sure you’ve installed the `requests` package first (`pip install requests`).  

Both approaches send exactly the same JSON you supplied, so either will work.

---

#### Common pitfalls & tips

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| “401 Unauthorized” error | Double‑check that the key hasn’t expired/been revoked. |
| “404 Not Found” | Verify the IP address is correct and that you’re hitting `/v3/...`. |
| Rate limits | VT may throttle repeated calls—wait a few seconds between retries. |
